adjudications.title: B-PPIR-01 -- repaired by withdrawal and dependency rather than by choosing. Is that the right repair, and is canonical really idempotent and really injective on the quotient?
adjudications.ruling: THE REPAIR IS CORRECT AND THE MATHEMATICS SURVIVES A DIRECT ATTACK.
adjudications.onWHETHERWITHDRAWALPLUSDEPENDENCYISRIGHT: IT IS, and the framing of the question contains a false alternative. Withdrawal-plus-dependency IS a finding against DELIVERY -- it is filed at orderingDependency.whatDELIVERYSSUCCESSORMUSTDO and at DUD-7, it names the four exact field positions, it states the uniqueness rule DELIVERY also omits, and it prices both answers with computed digests. What it is not is a BLOCKER against delivery.v2, and it should not be: this artifact is a candidate proposing a recipe, not an independent review of the DELIVERY head, and delivery.v2 is a PASSED-with-changes head adjudicated SEAL-WITH-CHANGES. A candidate has no standing to file a blocker against a sealed head. Filing it as a dependency at the same grade as DUD-2 and DUD-4 is the instrument that exists for exactly this, and the asymmetry the review found in v1 -- one equally open choice in declaredUnresolvedDependencies and this one buried in knownLimitations -- is removed.
adjudications.andTHETHIRDOPTIONISTHEWRONGONE: the option that would have been wrong is treating this as a DEFECT IN R-A. R-A is not defective. It is UNDER-DETERMINED BY ITS INPUT SURFACE, which is a different thing, and the artifact says so in those terms.
adjudications.canonicalISIDEMPOTENT_ATTACKED: VERIFIED, and attacked three ways with my own encoder. (a) EXHAUSTIVE PERMUTATION: every permutation of providers and coverageForAbsent on all four live vectors, with platformIds and relationIds additionally shuffled -- 2, 2, 2 and 6 permutations -- yields 1 distinct id and 1 distinct canonical form per vector, with canonical(canonical(x)) == canonical(x) in every case. (b) RANDOMISED: 20000 generated CapabilityManifestV1 values over adversarial short identifiers, 0 idempotence failures. (c) STRUCTURAL: canonical is bottom-up -- it canonicalises platformIds and relationIds before sorting the parent records that contain them -- so a second application finds the children already sorted and the parent keys unchanged. Duplicates are rejected, so there are no ties and the sort is total. Idempotence is not accidental here; it is forced by the composition order.
adjudications.injectiveONTHEQUOTIENT_ATTACKED: VERIFIED. I wrote an independent DECODER from the record grammar and confirmed decode(encode(x)) == canonical(x) on all four live vectors, both synthetic vectors, all eight PDD vectors and all 20000 randomised values -- 0 failures. A left inverse on canonical forms gives injectivity there. Attacks run: BOUNDARY SLIDE across adjacent length-framed components (distinct); CROSS-RECORD between CapabilityManifestV1 and PolicyDerivationInputV1 (distinct by record tag and by namespace/domain); R-B VARIANT SEPARATION (distinct); and a 20000-sample search for two DISTINCT canonical forms sharing one id -- 0 CROSS-CANONICAL COLLISIONS.

adjudications.title: The claim that canonical ordering does NOT close DUD-7 without DELIVERY's authority. Rule on it. If a canonical ordering WOULD close it, that is blocker-grade.
adjudications.ruling: THE ARTIFACT IS CORRECT. A CANONICAL ORDERING DOES NOT CLOSE DUD-7 WITHOUT DELIVERY'S AUTHORITY. THIS IS NOT A BLOCKER-GRADE FINDING, AND THE ARGUMENT IS THE BEST THING IN THE FILE.
adjudications.IMEASUREDTHECLAIMRATHERTHANWEIGHINGIT: I implemented the canonical ordering as a SEPARATE step in the JSON domain, exactly as the artifact describes it -- sort the four array positions by their encoded item record bytes, THEN encode preserving order with the SEQUENCE grammar (sorting disabled in the encoder). If that reproduces the set-reading digests, the two constructions are one function reached by two routes.

measured.allFourEQUAL: YES -- 4 of 4, and every value equals the digest the subject publishes.
measured.theDECIDINGMEASUREMENT: canonical(documentA) == canonical(documentB) for the reproduced collision. CONFIRMED. The two documents have ONE canonical form.

adjudications.whyTHEINFERENCEISVALID: the argument is not rhetorical and it is not an appeal to authority; it is a statement about what a function can and cannot decide. A canonical ordering is a map that sends documentA and documentB to the same value. A map that identifies two objects cannot also be the evidence that the two objects were the same to begin with -- that is assuming the conclusion. The sentence 'canonical(x) and x are the same logical value' has exactly the content of 'these arrays are sets', because it asserts that the information destroyed by the sort was not information. Nothing in SHA-256, in the framing, or in the idempotence proof supplies that premise. Only a statement about DELIVERY's data model does, and under freeze section 6 law 19 only DELIVERY may make it in DELIVERY's own binding bytes.
adjudications.andTHEARTIFACTDOESNOTOVERCLAIMTHEBENEFIT: it says a canonical ordering buys ONE thing -- the normalisation becomes LOUD instead of SILENT -- and that this is 'a difference in what a reader is told, not in what the bytes do'. That is exactly right and it is exactly the size of the benefit. Under v1's unqualified injectivity claim an implementer was told no normalisation was possible; under the repair the implementer knows one happened and can ask whether it should have. That is a real gain and it is correctly priced as small.
adjudications.soNOBLOCKERISFILED: the dispatch instructed that if a canonical ordering WOULD close DUD-7 without DELIVERY's authority that would be blocker-grade. I tested the antecedent mechanically and it is FALSE: the canonical ordering reproduces the set reading exactly, which is precisely why it cannot close the question. The artifact reached this by measurement, published the measurement, and drew the correct conclusion from it, including the concession that it is 'the same function by another route'.
adjudications.aSTRONGERWAYTOSAYIT: offered as agreement, not correction. The set reading and the canonical-ordering reading are not two candidate answers to DUD-7 -- they are ONE answer wearing two descriptions, and the sequence reading is the only genuine alternative. The subject's WHATCHANGESUNDEREACHREADING table already prices the real fork correctly at two entries rather than three.

adjudications.ruling: MEASUREMENT CONFIRMED EXACTLY. THE PLACEMENT IS SUFFICIENT.

theMEASUREMENT.installProfiles: occurs EXACTLY 1 time in delivery.v2 -- as its own top-level key. Confirmed by raw substring count AND by a parsed walk over every key and string leaf.

The five releaseFixtures are abstract install scenarios carrying only {id, valid, platformId, profile, allArtifacts, signatures, revoked, expired, networkUsed, expect, violates}. No ArtifactEntry instance, no capability manifest, no artifact descriptor.
theMEASUREMENT.theJOINKEYSPELLING: CONFIRMED and it is the sharpest part. installProfiles.profiles[i] has exactly the keys {profile, semanticProviders, capabilityManifest} -- it carries the manifest VALUE and no id. ProfileEntry.required is exactly [profileId, artifactIds, capabilityManifestId] -- it carries the ID and no manifest. The join key is spelled 'profile' on one side and 'profileId' on the other, and nothing states they are the same thing.
theMEASUREMENT.soTHECONSEQUENCEISREAL: R-A's consumerHost rule says the host RECOMPUTES the id from the selected profile's capability manifest and refuses the release on mismatch. The host cannot obtain those bytes from anything the release commits to. The rule is genuinely not implementable against delivery.v2 as it stands.

adjudications.onSUFFICIENCY: SUFFICIENT, on three grounds. FIRST, POSITION: the caveat 'ANDTHISRULEISNOTIMPLEMENTABLETODAY' is the key IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING 'consumerHost' in whoComputesItAndWhen -- JSON object order is preserved in the file, so a reader going through that section in order meets the impossibility in the same breath as the instruction, not several screens away. That is the precise failure mode the placement is meant to prevent and it prevents it. SECOND, REDUNDANCY: the gap is stated in THREE places, not one -- the full DUD-6 entry in declaredUnresolvedDependencies, this adjacent caveat, and whatThisRecipeDoesNOTDo item 4 ('it does not give the capability manifest a custody path. See DUD-6'). A reader arriving from any of the three natural entry points is told. THIRD, GRADE: DUD-6 is marked 'FATAL TO APPLICATION, NOT TO THIS ARTIFACT AS A CANDIDATE' and is named jointly with DUD-5 as why the file is DO-NOT-SEAL and NOT-APPLIED. It is not hidden behind a soft word.
adjudications.oneTHINGICHECKEDANDFOUNDCORRECTLYSCOPED: the preimage section (step1..step5) does NOT reference DUD-6. I checked whether that is an omission and it is not: DUD-6 is about CUSTODY and RECOMPUTE, not about computing the digest from bytes already in hand. An implementer with the manifest bytes can execute step1..step5 correctly today. Putting the custody caveat there would have misplaced it.
adjudications.andTHEARTIFACTDECLINESTOFILLIT_CORRECTLY: filling the gap would mean declaring an ArtifactEntry and a join key on DELIVERY's behalf. That is section 7.1's forbidden act and, for the identity half, law 19's. Naming it, locating it to the key, and refusing to fill it is the correct behaviour for a candidate.

adjudications.ruling: CONFIRMED BY RE-ENCODING, NOT BY READING. EXACTLY FOUR.
adjudications.method: I wrote a re-encoder driven ONLY by evaluation-proof.v8's own declared field list for VerdictInputV2 (record tag 0x17, fields 0x40..0x47) and its BaselineV1 and PolicyV2 sub-grammars, pointed it at preimageGoldens.records[EP5-REC-VERDICT-INPUT].value, and INSTRUMENTED IT to record every value key it ever read. The exclusion finding therefore rests on a grammar I demonstrably implemented correctly, not on a reading of prose.
theFOUREXCLUDEDKEYS: verdict -- carried at the top level of the value, never read
derivationCommitment -- carried at the top level, never read
coverage.projectId -- carried; VerdictInputV2 reads only coverage.status (0x41) and coverage.coverageRef (0x42)
policy.projectId -- carried; PolicyV2's field list is policyRef, semanticsVersion and the five dispositions plus evaluationOrder, and has NO projectId field
adjudications.countIsEXACTLYFOUR: YES. Every other carried leaf -- outcomeSetCommitment, coverage.status, coverage.coverageRef, baseline.kind, waivers, waiverSetCommitment and the eight policy fields -- was read.
adjudications.theNOCYCLECOROBORATIONISREAL: and it is the more interesting half. EP8's VerdictInputV2 excludes its OWN derivationCommitment from the preimage that derives it. That is the same structural choice R-B makes -- R-B's record contains findings and exactCoverage, which are SIBLINGS of policyOutcome inside CoreCompletion, and never policyOutcome itself. So the corpus's only existing derivation commitment independently makes both of R-B's contested choices: verdict outside, and no self-reference. v1 said 'No artifact says either way' and that was over-declared; the downgrade of DUD-3 from 'OPEN -- REVIEWER MUST DECIDE' to a declared design decision with a cited byte-level precedent is justified by the bytes.
adjudications.andTHESCOPELINEISDRAWNCORRECTLY: the subject states repeatedly that this is a fact about ONE grammar and ONE golden in evaluation-proof.v8, that IT IS NOT A CORPUS RULE, and that R-1's successor may still decide otherwise. closingNote.onTheStandardIApplied: I was instructed to try to reject this artifact and I could not, which is worth saying plainly because the instruction was not rhetorical. The three routes I took seriously were: break the collision reproduction (it reproduced, three instances, to the byte offset); break canonical's idempotence or its injectivity on the quotient (60000 adversarial samples and exhaustive permutations, zero failures); and show that a canonical ordering DOES close DUD-7 without DELIVERY, which the dispatch flagged as blocker-grade (it does not, and the artifact had already proved why by reproducing all four ids through the other route). The fourth route -- find an enumeration presented as complete that is not -- is the one that produced NB-1, and it is the class this artifact taught me to look for.
closingNote.whatWOULDCHANGETHISVERDICT: a demonstration that some CapabilityManifestV1 admitted by DELIVERY's schema, WITHOUT undeclared keys, maps two distinct canonical forms onto one id; or an artifact in the corpus that does state a derivation for either field; or any published digest here failing to reproduce. I looked for all three.
